Ingestion stage is structurally sound: split sizes (train 89 996 / val 10 004 / test 7 180) match the official PathMNIST manifest exactly, no subsampling was applied, all three index SHA-256 hashes are present, the archive MD5 and Zenodo data reference are recorded, and deterministic_torch is enabled with seed 42. The test-domain note (CRC-VAL-HE-7K images from a different clinical center) is correctly captured and should be carried into downstream evaluation interpretation.

One reproducibility gap warrants attention before later stages: llm_model_digest is null while llm_model is set to "qwen3.8" served via Ollama. If the LLM participates in any pipeline step (e.g., prompt-based labelling, augmentation selection, or qualitative evaluation), the absence of a weight digest means the exact model revision cannot be pinned or audited. Recommend that the run manifest be amended to record a concrete digest (SHA-256 of the GGUF/safetensors blob or the Ollama model tag with pull date) before the first LLM-dependent stage executes. The model identifier "qwen3.8" is also atypical relative to the usual Qwen naming scheme (qwen2.5, qwen3, …); verify it is the intended tag and not a typo for a different revision.

No deterministic findings were raised, no artefacts were omitted, and all package versions (torch 2.14.0+cu126, lightning 2.6.5, medmnist 3.0.2, numpy 2.4.6, scikit-learn 1.9.0, pydantic 2.13.5, jsonargparse 4.52.0) are internally consistent for a 2026-09 Linux x86_64 / Python 3.11.15 environment. Proceed to the next stage, but close the digest gap first.

llm_model identifier "qwen3.8" is atypical for the Qwen naming convention; confirm it is the intended tag and not a typo
Test split originates from a different clinical center (domain shift); ensure downstream evaluation reports this explicitly to avoid over-optimistic generalisation claims
